I had a great time in Conan. My highlight is playing it with the old Arnold films on for background noise. I don't have any major complaints about the game. If you haven't played it yet, a few words of advice: 1) While you can play the game single player, it is very much a multiplayer game. Forward progress is hindered when its just you and a minion against bigger and stronger enemies. So, if you go solo look into getting some mods to help you out. 2) Real estate is key. Pick you base(s) carefully. Lots of guides out there to help with that. 3) Weather is a thing (not too much of a spoiler).

Enjoy!

Survival game that doesn't hold your hand. It took a while to understand the game and how to play but payed off in the end. I'm happy with my purchase. If you like sandbox survival games this has got to be one for you to buy.

In a world full of Arks, Rusts, The Forests, and more, you've got Conan.

It has its own flavor, its own style, and of all of them I think the strongest in terms of combat. It's got a lot of cool history to draw on, but from what I understand, even though Conan the Barbarian was cool in its time, it doesn't have the staying power of other, more popular fantasy series. I never knew the story of Conan. Being a big story nerd typically, I am judging this on pure game play and setting, which in my opinion is far above the other games in this genre. It's not as popular, and not near as moddable as ARK (Which lets be real, is the ONLY reason Ark survived.) But it's not bad base mechanics of these genres considered. If you like the history, get it for sure, if you just want a survival game that makes more sense than the others, this one does it for me there, too.

I have enjoyed Conan Exiles. I like that you can go it solo or you can team up. I also love the building aspect of the game. What I don't like is the need for consist maintenance or lose everything. Life happens and you may need to leave the game for a week or more. If you return, all that you have is a naked barbarian.

It's a nice game. It still feels very unstable and there are still loads of bugs. The ones that spring to the eye most are half decayed buildings, stuff hanging in mid air, etc. Also the crafting system needs to follow a more logical path. As it is now some things make no sense at all. I feel like there is loads of work to be done but it looks very promising and I feel we will arrive at an awesome game once every aspect of it is balanced and fixed. Keep at it Funcom! Don't disapoint your early supporters!

Love this game and how variable it can be. There's some things that don't always work like they should, but having played many top end MMOs or group content based games, it's about the same kind of stuff you run into anywhere. There's a great sense of ambience and while it can be a single player type adventure, it is truly a very co-op friendly game. No group size restrictions, just get your friends and go see whatever you want. I love the building aspect and hunting for new feats and just the general open exploration. The game can be punishing for failing, but it really forces you to be mindful about choices and how you engage something. That being said, it feels good when you prepare and take down content that was terrifying before and then you kick it in the teeth XD If you're looking for a solid, sandbox game that's co-op friendly, I highly recommend.

Best survival game since DayZ Epoch. Yes, it doesn't have vehicles or guns. Yes, it has its fair share of bugs and weird design decision. But it's a sandbox game where you always have something to do or someone to kill.

I don't condone selling paid DLCs with so little content, but a dev studio needs to satisfy its owners' insatiable appetites, and if that makes the game survive year after year, you won't see me complain.

Pros: One of the most immersive experiences ever. Sound design, music, and open world are very good. Feels like an adventure in a way that many games fail to capture. Gathering, building, survival mechanics are well-done. Dungeons are dark and ominous in a good way. Captures the spirit and tone of Conan (and the R.Howard universe). The enhanced version brings it all to a new level.

Cons: Boss and enemy movement and mechanics can be a bit janky. Crocs don't swim (not sure why this has persisted)? Wish there were boats and fishing. My friends won't play it (not sure why).

-Latest Patch prevents Player from starting the game if any mods is in opinion of game outdated (crazy never had that in any game, why would you prevent the use of outdated mods?????)

If you are a fan of the Conan mythos, there is much to enjoy about this game, which samples widely but tells it's own unique story. If you are a fan of open world exploration and survival, this game is also a fun way to pass a few hours. Whether you are focusing on the grind in order to build your best base in one of the beautifully rendered locations, or just hack/slashing your way through the biomes and dungeons. Yes, there are glitches (kill a rhino, watch it fly), and it may not be as sophisticated as other open worlders, but I still get a lot of pleasure from jumping int the Exiled Lands and staying not dead.
(Clarification: I play single player; this review does not apply to multiplayer experiences or the to Septah expansion, neither of which I have experienced)

Do the Journey Steps and you're practically done with the game.

Pros
-Standard survival elements (resource management, gathering, crafting, taming Thralls).
-It's in the Conan universe.
-Each content patch has been timely and noticeable enhancements of the game.
-Each server I have played on was nearly full of solid gamers (the occasional troll).
-Modding community is growing.
-Patching soon to Unreal Engine 4.15 - this is a really big deal for modders, enabling us to create content with modern workflows.
-THE ROLEPLAYING Survival game. Incredible work as gone into the Emote System and general Roleplay needs.

Cons
-Combat feels loose, but once you're used to it you can perform just fine.
-Tech curve is STEEP on Official servers. Can be avoided by just tweaking numbers / running mods on unofficial servers.
-Progression feels slow, but again, can be avoided if not on Official servers.

Pros

-Nice graphics
-Conan IP
-Tittays
-Music is alrightish

Cons

-Incredibly similar to Ark, in terms of both gameplay and progression
-Host of connectivity issues
-Host of graphical issues and anomalies
-Server selection oly works a quarter of the time

Aside from the graphical and connectivity issues, which I assume will be addressed in the near future, this game just doesn't pop out at me. Outside of character creation, I had the most overwhelming sense that I was playing Ark again, and that was confirmed for me by the progression through crafting and building which is almost copy and paste.

I'm sure the game will improve over time, at least I hope so. I'll continue watching to see if it gets better, but for now, I have to give it a thumbs down. This kind of a game with a Conan IP is nice, but it's not enough.

This game has had many ups and downs over the years. There are some glaring flaws in their battle pass, ingame shop, and some of their DLC. That being said, I still think Conan Exiles is worth your time. It is one of the best survival games in existence. Despite its flaws, the building in the game is incredibly detailed. The combat is fun and the PvE progression is awesome. Item drop rates are perfect. Respawn timers are perfect. I preferred the thrall system before the crafting overhaul, but even though it isn't as great as it once was, it's still a solid 8/10. If you're tired of other survival games but you still want to fight, farm resources, and build an empire, give Conan Exiles a shot.

Started out a bit weak, but has progressively improved to the point that with some of the more interesting addon's like Pippi, you could really create a great Conan like world for your friends to play, or the public for that matter. But you do need to invest in the content packs to get the full enjoyment...so it's a bit bigger investment than it may seem on the surface. Great fun though!

I've played it only solo and declining the anti-cheat program.

I loved the crafting and exploring, combat is okay, ambience is nice.
It is highly possible I reinstall the game to spend more time in it.

Cons:
- some (non-breaking) bugs (found at least 3, related to climbing, building and sprinting)
- some CRASHING bugs (found one with the inventory, please avoid double clicking stuff in there, and drag&drop instead)
- lack of explanation (you are left in a desert where you can't build nothing, and not told you have a map... so I wasted my early time in the game trying to put a bedroll on the ground and it just would not let me do it of course). This is the most annoying example I can come up with, but other bits of explanation here and there would have been nice.

Overall, despite the 3 inventory crashes and the other cons, I really enjoyed this game. Was chill and I really liked discovering Conan's universe this way.
